headline: UK Job Vacancies Drop to 12-Year Low of 690,000 as Wage Growth Cools
summary: UK job vacancies fell by 22,000 in August to October to 690,000, reaching their lowest level in 12 years excluding pandemic lockdowns, while wage growth slowed alongside lower unemployment.
why: The Bank of England monitors labor slack and wage increases to assess domestic inflationary pressure and guide interest rate policy.

impacts.name: British Pound
impacts.why: Cooling wage growth and a 12-year low in job vacancies bolster expectations of Bank of England rate reductions.
